newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Italian named in Bofors probe denies involvement.
newsitem.headline: Italian named in Bofors probe denies involvement.

text.p: An Italian national named by investigators as a recipient of payments from Swedish gun manufacturer Bofors in a $1.3 billion gun deal with India on Friday denied any involvement in the affair.
In a statement issued in Kuala Lumpur, Ottavio Quattrocchi, who worked for Italian engineering firm Snamprogetti in India, said he had no connection "with the Bofors affair".

"I wish to state emphatically and unequivocally that no relationship whatsoever has ever existed at any point in time between me and Bofors and consequently between me, Bofors and India or any Indian nationals," he said in the statement.
India's Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on February 12 named Quattrocchi and his wife Maria among five people who it said had received payments from Bofors.
"The CBI is taking necessary steps to take action against the persons involved," CBI said in a statement. It did not elaborate.

Quattrocchi was the Indian representative of Snamprogetti SpA when the artillery contract between Bofors AB, a unit of Swedish defence group Celsius, and the Indian government was signed in 1986. He now lives in Malaysia.
Swiss police have said there was evidence Bofors paid about $40 million into various banks accounts in Switzerland during the time the contract with India was drawn up and settled.
Blaming the Indian media for linking him to the Bofors issue, he said he would take legal measures if necessary.
"I will take all such legal measures as may be necessary in India and/or in any other appropriate forums to defend my reputation," he said in the statement.
